_strings.@@097b7c5105c0: Tuition and Textbook Credit (K-12) — A parent/taxpayer who claims a dependent attending grades K-12 at an accredited Iowa school (nonprofit, Civil-Rights-Act-adherent) or receiving qualifying private instruction (Iowa Code 422.12), and who paid tuition and textbook expenses for that dependent. Only the spouse/parent claiming a given dependent may claim that dependent's expenses; expenses paid with 529-account distributions may qualify. NEW for 2024 — purchases made from Students First Educational Savings Account (ESA) funds under Iowa Code 257.11B are NOT eligible.
_strings.@@12808e7464d1: 2024 IA 1040 Expanded Instructions (archived PDF) — What's New (bracket rate decreases; 2025 single rate 3.8%; Schedule 1 renumbering; ISave 529 limit $5,500; federal tax refund reporting ends), Who Must File thresholds, low-income exemption, line 5 tax / 5.7% alternate tax over $13,500/$32,000, exemption credits, line 9 tuition and textbook credit, line 24 child and dependent care / early childhood credits, line 25 EITC 15%, rounding rules
_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@1c8d9d29cc11: Early Childhood Development Credit — Residents with Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 4) of less than $90,000 who paid qualifying early childhood development expenses for a dependent aged three through five. Claimed in lieu of (not in addition to) the Child and Dependent Care Credit — only one of the two may be taken per year. For married separate filers the $90,000 limit applies only to the income of the spouse claiming the dependent.
_strings.@@223829bb6c75: Low-Income Exemption (with elevated threshold for filers age 65+) — This is an exemption from Iowa income tax (not a dollar-amount credit) functioning as Iowa's primary low-income and senior relief on the IA 1040 — Iowa has no separate 'elderly credit' line. A taxpayer is exempt from Iowa income tax if Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 4, with required add-backs incl. the line 1d standard/itemized deduction, line 1e QBI deduction, lump-sum distributions, and the Schedule 1 line 17 NOL carryover) is at or below the threshold for their filing status. Senior filers (taxpayer or spouse 65 or older on 12/31/24) qualify under a substantially higher threshold. The 2024 IA 1040 Schedule 1 prints line 17 as one box, "Iowa net operating loss prior to 1/1/23. Include IA 124" (page 5, 41-001e; https://revenue.iowa.gov/media/4090/download?inline); the Expanded Instructions p.10 add-back list still reads "Carryover of net operating loss claimed on the IA 1040 Schedule 1, line 17b", while p.5 ("Who Must File?") reads "line 17" and the p.12 alternate tax worksheet reads "line 17, column B".

_strings.@@37fe6af9ddae: IA 126 (Iowa Nonresident and Part-Year Resident Credit Schedule), form number 41-126, filed together with the IA 1040. (Iowa does not use a separate nonresident return; nonresidents/part-year residents file the IA 1040 and attach the IA 126.)

_strings.@@41bd77081ef8: Treaty conformity — IA conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from IA income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the IA return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Iowa conforms. The 2024 IA 1040 keeps the 2023 redesign's starting point — "federal taxable income" — with Step 4 computing Iowa taxable income as federal taxable income (IA 1040 line 2, from federal 1040 line 15) plus net Iowa modifications from IA 1040 Schedule 1 (line 3, from Schedule 1 line 21 for 2024). Lines 1a-1e (federal total income, adjustments, AGI, standard/itemized deduction, QBI deduction) are printed for reference only ("Do not include lines 1a through 1e"). Iowa applies rolling IRC conformity. Federally treaty-exempt income is excluded from federal AGI/federal taxable income before it ever reaches the Iowa return, and there is NO treaty/foreign-income re-inclusion among the 2024 Schedule 1 Column A additions (interest from non-exempt state/municipal securities, certain dividends, partnership/S-corp modifications, depreciation/Section 179 nonconformity, and NOL carryforward items). This is reinforced by Iowa Admin. Code rule 701—300.17, which states a resident is taxed on all income "except when an item of income is specifically exempted from taxation by a provision of federal or Iowa law." Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed.

_strings.@@5c364b3bc55e: Iowa Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — Available only to taxpayers who qualify for the federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC). Iowa simply piggybacks on federal EITC eligibility (earned income, AGI, investment-income, and qualifying-child rules are determined at the federal level). A taxpayer who qualifies for the Iowa low-income exemption may file an Iowa return solely to claim a refund of this credit (check the alternate-tax / low-income-exemption box the 2024 IA 1040 face prints under the Step 5 heading, above line 5 — the Expanded Instructions p.44 still call it "the box between Steps 4 and 5" — skip lines 5-19, enter zero on lines 20 and 22, and enter the EITC on lines 25, 30, 31a, and 32). The 2024 face splits line 31 into 31a (overpayment) and 31b ("AMENDED RETURN ONLY. Previous refunds."); the p.44 EITC-only paragraph still says "lines 25, 30, 31, and 32" while p.53 documents 31a/31b. An original (non-amended) return leaves 31b blank, so line 32 equals line 31a. (2024 IA 1040 fillable form 41-001, page 2 (41-001b) Step 5 checkbox and page 3 (41-001c) lines 31a/31b/32, https://revenue.iowa.gov/media/4090/download?inline; 2024 IA 1040 Expanded Instructions pp.44 and 53, https://revenue.iowa.gov/media/4152/download?inline)
_strings.@@74917c13b93d: 2024 IA 1040 (form 41-001) printed footer: 'This return is due April 30, 2025'; Iowa DOR Individual Taxes page: 'Iowa tax returns are due April 30.' Iowa's individual due date is April 30, NOT the federal April 15.
_strings.@@7e89764a21d3: Iowa Department of Revenue — 2024 Tax Calculation Worksheet (41-026): NON-JOINT FILERS (filing status 1, 3, 4, or 5) $0-$6,210 at 4.40% (.044), $6,210-$31,050 at 4.82% (.0482) plus $273.24, $31,050-and-over at 5.70% (.057) plus $1,470.53; JOINT FILERS (filing status 2) $0-$12,420 at 4.40%, $12,420-$62,100 at 4.82% plus $546.48, $62,100-and-over at 5.70% plus $2,941.06; worked example $25,000 non-joint -> $1,178.92. Second pass: 2024 IA 1040 (41-001) Step 4 'Iowa taxable income. Add lines 2 and 3. Do not include lines 1a through 1e' (line 2 = federal taxable income from federal 1040 line 15; line 3 = net Iowa modifications from IA 1040 Schedule 1, line 21) and Step 5 line 5 'Iowa tax from tax rate schedule or alternate tax', Step 3 $40/$20/$40 exemption CREDITS; 2024 IA 1040 Expanded Instructions — What's New: 'Line 5: The tax rates for each tax bracket have decreased. For tax year 2025, Iowa will have a single tax rate of 3.8%' (the flat rate begins TY2025, NOT TY2024); alternate tax = 5.7% of income over $13,500/$32,000 — both passes agree.
_strings.@@8aa830d0e140: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): ALTERNATE TAX PERCENTAGE DROPPED to 5.7% (.057) for 2024, down from 6% in 2023: all filing statuses except single may compute the alternate tax on the alternate-tax-worksheet income above $13,500 ($32,000 if the taxpayer or spouse was 65 or older on 12/31/2024) and enter the SMALLER of that or the rate-schedule tax on IA 1040 line 5 (status-3 spouses prorate it). Resolve via: 2024 IA 1040 Expanded Instructions, line 5 alternate-tax instructions at the citation URL (and the Iowa Income Tax Reduction Worksheet 41-146 for single filers).
_strings.@@b38e348255ba: Child and Dependent Care Credit — Residents with Iowa taxable income (IA 1040 line 4) of less than $90,000 who paid qualifying child/dependent care expenses and qualify for the federal child and dependent care credit (must include completed federal Form 2441). For married filing jointly, both spouses' Iowa taxable income is combined to test the $90,000 limit. Only one of the Child & Dependent Care Credit OR the Early Childhood Development Credit may be claimed per year. Generally cannot be claimed if filing status is married filing separately (see IRS Pub. 503).

_strings.@@f546644cecfa: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): IA 1040 SCHEDULE 1 MODIFICATIONS REWORKED for 2024: the schedule was renumbered (net modifications now line 21, military retirement exclusion now line 4), a NEW surviving-spouse pension exemption and a NEW exemption for 529-to-Roth transfers were added, the ISave 529 deduction limit is $5,500 per beneficiary, federal income tax refunds received in 2024 and later are no longer reported, and two checkoffs were repealed. Separately, purchases made from Students First Educational Savings Account (ESA) funds under Iowa Code 257.11B became NOT eligible for the tuition and textbook credit. Resolve via: 2024 IA 1040 Schedule 1 and its instructions inside the 2024 IA 1040 Expanded Instructions at the citation URL; the net modification amount is the filer's own Schedule 1 line 21.

Tax line: IA 1040 (41-001) Step 5, line 5: 'Iowa tax from tax rate schedule or alternate tax' — computed on IA 1040 line 4 'Iowa taxable income' via the 2024 Tax Calculation Worksheet (41-026) or the IA 1040 Tax Calculator (line 4 = line 2 federal taxable income + line 3 net Iowa modifications; 'Do not include lines 1a through 1e'). This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 schedule change (VERIFIED): the four 2023 brackets consolidated to THREE — the 6.00% top bracket is gone and 5.70% now applies to all income over $31,050 (non-joint) / $62,100 (joint); bracket bounds indexed up from $6,000/$30,000 and $12,000/$60,000. Iowa's single flat rate of 3.8% (SF 2442) begins TAX YEAR 2025 — do NOT apply it to 2024. Base guidance: supply 2024 IA 1040 line 4 'Iowa taxable income' = line 2 federal taxable income (federal 1040, line 15) + line 3 net Iowa modifications (IA 1040 Schedule 1, line 21 — renumbered from line 22 in 2023). Lines 1a-1e (federal total income, adjustments, AGI, standard/itemized deduction, QBI deduction) are printed for reference only. The federal standard/itemized deduction and QBI deduction are already inside federal taxable income — Iowa has no state standard deduction or base personal exemptions, and this op subtracts nothing before the schedule. Two schedules only: the 2024 Tax Calculation Worksheet (41-026) prints one schedule for JOINT filers (Iowa filing status 2) and one for NON-JOINT filers (statuses 1, 3, 4, and 5) — single, married filing separately, and head of household ship the identical non-joint schedule; married_filing_jointly ships the joint schedule. CRITICAL — qualifying surviving spouse: Iowa status 5 (qualifying surviving spouse) is a NON-JOINT filer on the 41-026 worksheet, but this op's status aliasing resolves qualifying-surviving-spouse to the married_filing_jointly schedule, which would UNDERSTATE Iowa tax. For an Iowa QSS filer, pass filing_status='single' (the identical non-joint schedule). Printed-constant rounding (quantified): the 2024 top-bracket Column C constants are the exact cumulative sums rounded to the CENT — non-joint $1,470.53 vs exact $1,470.528 (+$0.002), joint $2,941.06 vs exact $2,941.056 (+$0.004); the first constants ($273.24 / $546.48) are exact. This op does exact marginal math, so worksheet results can exceed it by less than half a cent — immaterial after whole-dollar rounding. Cents vs whole dollars: the IA 1040 is captioned 'Enter Dollars and Cents' and the worksheet computes tax to the cent; whole-dollar rounding is OPTIONAL ('To round, drop amounts under 50 cents and increase amounts from 50 to 99 cents to the next dollar' — a .50 tie rounds UP, matching this op). No tax-table mandate: all filers use the 41-026 worksheet or the online IA 1040 Tax Calculator. Exemption CREDITS, not base exemptions (NOT modeled): IA 1040 Step 3 computes personal credits at $40 (enter 1 for statuses 1, 3, and 5; 2 for statuses 2 and 4), $20 per 65-or-older (on or before January 1, 2025) or blind condition, and $40 per dependent; the Step 3 total is a CREDIT against tax on line 8 — never a base reduction. exemptions ships empty; pass exemptions_count=0 and dependents_count=0. Alternate tax (NOT modeled): all statuses except single may compute an alternate tax — 5.7% (.057) for 2024 (down from 6% in 2023) of the alternate-tax-worksheet income above $13,500 ($32,000 if you or your spouse was 65 or older on 12/31/2024) — and enter the SMALLER amount on line 5 (check the Step 5 box); status-3 spouses prorate it. Single taxpayers may instead qualify for the Iowa Income Tax Reduction Worksheet (41-146). Check these when income is just above the threshold. Low-income exemption (NOT modeled): filers whose Iowa taxable income plus specified add-backs is at or below $9,000 (single/married filing separately; $24,000 if 65+ on 12/31/24), or $13,500 (married filing jointly / head of household / qualifying surviving spouse; $32,000 if 65+), owe no Iowa income tax (check the box the 2024 IA 1040 prints under the Step 5 heading, above line 5: "Check if using alternate tax (line 5), tax reduction calculation (line 12), or low-income exemption. See instructions." The Expanded Instructions p.44 still call it "the box between Steps 4 and 5"); a dependent filer's threshold is $5,000; MFS also requires combined income of $13,500 or less. Not modeled — later lines: Iowa lump-sum tax (line 6), the Step 3 exemption credits (line 8), tuition and textbook credit (line 9 — 2024: Students First ESA purchases not eligible), volunteer firefighter/EMS/reserve peace officer credit (line 10), the IA 126 nonresident/part-year credit (line 13), out-of-state tax credit (line 15), SCHOOL DISTRICT SURTAX and EMS surtax (line 19, in Step 5: "School district surtax or EMS surtax. Multiply line 18 by the percentage from list"; Step 6 is "Refundable Credits and Payments", lines 23-30), the 15%-of-federal Iowa EITC (line 25), and the child and dependent care / early childhood development credits (line 24).
